_readme: DECLARATIVE ANTI-DRIFT ARTIFACT. No Early Clock-Out calculation engine exists in
this repository and none was implemented. These vectors are NOT executed.
§42: 'These vectors are normative. They ship as executable fixtures and MUST pass
before release and on every subsequent build.' Defect D-21 records why they exist:
'A deterministic engine specified without golden vectors will be implemented as
several mutually incompatible variants.'
They are committed BEFORE any engine so that expected outputs cannot later be bent
to match whatever an implementation happens to produce. That is the whole point.
RULES FOR ANYONE EDITING THIS FILE:
* 'scenario', 'inputs_verbatim' and 'expected_verbatim' are transcribed from the
§42 table character-for-character. They are the authority. Do not reword, do not
normalise punctuation, do not 'clarify'.
* 'expected_fields' is a convenience structuring of values the specification states
explicitly. Where the specification is prose, the field is omitted rather than
interpreted. On any disagreement, 'expected_verbatim' wins.
* 'harness' is execution metadata ONLY. It records why a vector cannot run yet.
Changing a harness field never changes a normative expectation.
* Weakening an expected output to make an implementation pass is defect D-21.
Amending a vector requires the specification owner, not the implementer.
BLOCKING DEPENDENCY CODES (from the three-phase read-only audit):
P-1  sealed state interval ledger + ledger_version           (absent)
P-2  deterministic classifier, BRK_M/BRK_R distinct states   (absent)
P-3  clock-out provenance: genuine vs system-synthesized     (absent)
P-4  minute-granular leave                                   (absent)
P-5  historically resolvable policy versioning               (absent)
C-2  fail-closed REQUIREMENT_UNRESOLVED state                (unreachable today)
MODEL-NETTING  netting/banking model                         (absent platform-wide)
MODEL-GRACE    grace_minutes on the requirement model        (absent)
MODEL-HORIZON  retroactive-horizon setting                   (absent)
MODEL-WORKWEEK workweek-start + shift-attribution settings   (absent)

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Req 525; WRK 270+225; BRK_M 45 unpaid; leave 17:30–18:00; sched end 18:30
vectors.expected_verbatim: variance −60; qualifying 495; gross 30; excluded 30; attributable 0; no event

harness.note: Requires sealed intervals and a 30-minute leave window (17:30–18:00). Both exist: the producer seals intervals, and Step 7's leave_interval capability represents intraday boundaries, which app/eval_day/exclusion.py already consumes. MODEL-VARIANCE closed under owner rulings D-1.1 and D-2.1: the scheduled end is resolved once at seal and frozen on the ledger with its source tier, and §18 step 14 computes the variance from that frozen evidence alone.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Req 525; BRK_R 15 + 20 with cap 30; BRK_M 45 unpaid
vectors.expected_verbatim: qualifying 500; attributable 25; rest capped at 30 cumulative

harness.note: §19.1: rest is capped cumulatively, not per interval — two 20-minute rest breaks against a 30-minute cap qualify 20 + 10, not 20 + 20.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Same ledger as GV-02 evaluated with a single break category
vectors.expected_verbatim: MUST FAIL. Asserts that no code path collapses BRK_M and BRK_R (INV-4)

harness.note: Cannot even be EXPRESSED today: the platform has one generic break bucket (break_sessions.break_type is a worker-selected 'break'|'lunch' label, and all break types are subtracted equally), so there are not two states to collapse. This vector is the direct guard against the D-01 defect.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Prior week 20; today gross 10, no exclusion
vectors.expected_verbatim: weekly 30; crossed = true; one ECO_THRESHOLD_REACHED

harness.note: §21.1: the comparison is W(w,k) >= T(t,k). Exactly 30 triggers; strictly-greater-than is a defect. The fold arithmetic is pure, but the day records it folds do not exist.

vectors.expected_verbatim: weekly 29; crossed = false; no event

vectors.inputs_verbatim: GV-04 then further shortfalls to 36 and 44
vectors.expected_verbatim: Exactly one primary event; no further notifications

harness.note: §21.2: created by natural key (tenant_id, worker_id, workweek_key, tier='PRIMARY'), not by a 'has notified' boolean, so a replay cannot create a second.

vectors.expected_verbatim: weekly 20; ECO_THRESHOLD_WITHDRAWN emitted; original retained; both recipients notified

harness.note: R-21.3.1: the original event is never deleted, never back-dated, never hidden. ALERT-DELIVERY is satisfied: the notification platform (D-A), the persist-first processing step (D-C) and the operational command (D-F) deliver per recipient and record the returned DispatchResult. Both original recipients are reached from the FROZEN snapshot, a repeated pass retransmits nothing under D-4, and the withdrawal reaches the same recipients after current authority is removed.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: GV-07 then a further 12 min shortfall
vectors.expected_verbatim: weekly 32; new primary event with sequence = 2 referencing the withdrawal
One work_date = Sunday; minutes counted once; accrues to the week containing Sunday

harness.note: R-12.3.5: a shift may never be attributed to two workweeks. No shift-attribution setting exists.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Shift 01:00–10:00 local on a transition day, Europe/London
vectors.expected_verbatim: Duration 8h, not 9h; required minutes unchanged at 525

harness.note: §16.3: required minutes are a duration, not a wall-clock span. app/_tz already resolves through the IANA zone; the interval set to measure does not exist.

vectors.expected_verbatim: Week boundary correct; week is 169 hours; no day double-counted

harness.note: §24.8: any implementation that assumes 168 hours will drift twice a year. The workweek-start setting now exists (schedule.week_start_day, W4).

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Five days each 36s short of requirement
vectors.expected_verbatim: Five daily shortfalls of 1 min; weekly total 5, not 3

harness.note: R-16.5: weekly totals are the sum of ROUNDED daily minutes. Requires per-day qualifying SECONDS, which no table stores.

vectors.expected_verbatim: excluded 15; attributable 15

harness.note: The specification notes the withdrawn draft covered only full coverage; partial coverage 'is the common one and was undefined (defect D-22)'. Leave is date-granular here.

vectors.expected_verbatim: excluded 30; attributable 0; never negative
attributable 0; no credit created

harness.note: §14.2 Example D: leave does not create credit.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: No clock-out interval for the day
vectors.expected_verbatim: state MISSING_CLOCK_OUT; no shortfall; no advisory; contributes 0

harness.note: P-3 is the distinctive blocker; P-1 is listed because this vector's own input is stated in terms of the interval set ('No clock-out interval for the day') and §19 step 7 tests hasNoClockOut against sealed intervals loaded at step 5. §7.2 calls inferring an end of day 'the single worst thing this control could do'. Two auto-close paths synthesize clock_out_time (local end-of-day; last heartbeat, or clock-in time if none was ever seen) and clock_sessions carries no column distinguishing them from a genuine departure.

vectors.expected_verbatim: state DEFERRED_PENDING_LEDGER; contributes 0; visible to both parties; recomputes on resolution

harness.note: §24.7: the day is 'neither counted nor excused'. The canonical status Unverified Exit — Pending Review does not exist in this platform.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: No requirement at any of the six ranks
vectors.expected_verbatim: state REQUIREMENT_UNRESOLVED; admin alert; nothing shown to the Worker

harness.note: REQUIREMENT_UNRESOLVED is REACHABLE. app.requirement_resolution returns it when configuration exists and no rank answers usably, and EVAL-DAY maps it to EcoDayState.REQUIREMENT_UNRESOLVED with shortfall_computed false. The rank-6 fail-open default in attendance_policy.resolve_expected_work_seconds is a separate legacy path the strict resolver deliberately does not fall through to. ALERT was a STALE citation, not a satisfied one: a requirement-unresolved day emits no threshold event, so ALERT's entry point could never fire for it — the same error owner ruling B3 corrected for GV-17. Ruling 2: B authorized a separate day-scoped primitive instead, and app.eco_day_alert raises the §24.3 alert from the authoritative EcoDayRecord to the designated PRIMARY ADMIN under the non-suppressible ECO_ADMIN_OPERATIONAL class.

vectors.expected_verbatim: Tuesday attributable 20

harness.note: MODEL-NETTING closed under owner rulings D-6.3/D-6.4/D-6.8 through D-6.12. Netting is consumed at §18 step 10, before gross and before exclusions; NONE creates and consumes nothing, which is what makes this vector diverge from GV-20.

vectors.expected_verbatim: Tuesday attributable 0; bank consumed 20

harness.note: MODEL-NETTING closed under owner rulings D-6.3/D-6.4/D-6.8 through D-6.12. The bank is a FOLD over day records (§15.1 / INV-3) — no counter, balance or period row exists — and the per-day and per-period caps come from the governing PolicyVersion. PERIOD_BANK remains refused: §15 suspends weekly evaluation under it and no reference period is recorded anywhere.

vectors.expected_verbatim: required 510, in perpetuity

harness.note: app_settings is a mutable key/value store with updated_at only — no version, no effective_from, no history — so a historical day re-resolves against current policy.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Correction in week k+2 pushes week k to 33
vectors.expected_verbatim: Event with is_retroactive = true; copy names the workweek and cause

harness.note: §21.5: the notification MUST NOT read as though the condition arose today.

vectors.expected_verbatim: Record corrected; no notification

harness.note: §21.5: a threshold notification about a week five months ago 'has no legitimate operational purpose and reads as harassment'. MODEL-HORIZON closed under owner rulings D-7.1 and D-7.2: elapsed days are LOCAL calendar dates in the workweek's frozen timezone, the boundary is strictly greater-than, and the horizon comes from the PolicyVersion governing the corrected week. The decision is notification ELIGIBILITY only — the record is still corrected, which is why record_corrected and notification_sent are independent here.

vectors.expected_verbatim: attributable zeroed to 0; gross retained as 3 in the record

harness.note: §11: grace_minutes exists so tenants do not get it implemented 'as a magic number in the threshold comparison, which is where it does the most damage'. The requirement model has no grace field.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Replay every event in the fixture set twice
vectors.expected_verbatim: Identical final state; no duplicate events, records or notifications

harness.note: Day-evaluation natural key is (tenant, worker, work_date, ledger_version, policy_version) — two of the five components do not exist.

vectors.expected_verbatim: state LEDGER_INTEGRITY_FAULT; no evaluation; incident raised; no clamping

harness.note: The ECO path already refused: work_ledger.integrity detects OVERLAPPING_INTERVALS, the producer records LEDGER_INTEGRITY_FAULT, and EVAL-DAY raises EvaluationRefused rather than repairing, clamping or skipping it. The legacy union in employees.router._actual_break_seconds_for_sessions protects a dashboard number and is not on this path. §24.15 — 'Silently coping with corrupt evidence is how evidentiary systems lose their standing.' Both citations are now resolved. STATE-CONTRACT is satisfied by the existing D-8.1 contract: LedgerState is authoritative for ledger facts, LedgerState.LEDGER_INTEGRITY_FAULT already exists, and EcoDayState remains the seven-member evaluation vocabulary — no new evaluation state was introduced. ALERT was a STALE citation, not a satisfied one: §24.15 asks for a platform INCIDENT, which is operational evidence that a Tenant ledger holds a defect — it has no audience, no recipient, no channel and no delivery, it emits no threshold event and it is not routed through app/alert. Owner ruling D-9.1 authorized a dedicated primitive instead, and app.eco_ledger_incident raises the incident from the authoritative ledger fault identity, exactly once per fault version, append-only under R5.

vectors.expected_verbatim: Per-day requirements 240/240/525/525/525; single weekly threshold

harness.note: The REQUIREMENT half of this vector is the closest to satisfiable today: the Schedule Resolver already resolves per Worker per date and carries a provenance 'sources' map, so per-day 240/240/525/525/525 is representable. The vector still cannot execute, because a day record needs qualifying minutes to sit beside the requirement.

vectors.inputs_verbatim: Rest day with an accidental clock-in
vectors.expected_verbatim: required 0; gross 0; no advisory; day record written as NOT_A_WORKING_DAY

harness.note: EffectiveSchedule.is_working_day already answers the working-day question; the day record the specification requires 'so that the week fold is complete and explainable' is now written — a dedicated classifier owns the determination, the producer freezes its verdict into the ledger state, and EVAL-DAY zeroes the day from that frozen context.
